answer: Verifiable delay functions curb Sybil attacks by requiring agents to evaluate non-parallelizable sequential puzzles. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated wall-clock compute time and power per identity, emitting an authentic cryptographic signal rather than a cloned echo. Even at the zenith of hardware efficiency, unparallelized time cannot be compressed. However, this delay penalizes time-sensitive autonomous agents and advantages attackers operating specialized ASICs.
